title: Spin fluctuations and nearly isotropic quasiparticles in the doped three-dimensional Hubbard model
authors: Pengcheng Hou, Kun Chen, Youjin Deng
abstract: Away from half filling and above its Neel temperature, the three-dimensional Hubbard model is a paramagnetic metal with antiferromagnetic spin fluctuations, where controlled momentum-resolved results have been lacking. Using connected-determinant diagrammatic Monte Carlo, we compute the momentum-resolved self-energy for n = 0.4-0.95, T/t = 0.05-0.33 and U/t = 4-8, and the full-zone spin susceptibility at twelve of these points, focusing on U/t = 4. At U/t = 4 and toward half filling the spin fluctuations become strong: for n = 0.7-0.9 at T/t = 0.14 they enhance the susceptibility peak up to sevenfold and raise the momentum-dependent part of the scattering rate to four to five times its second-order value. They are driven by an effective spin interaction screened to about 2U/3 and nearly uniform over the zone. Yet the peak height is set by the slightly smaller value of this interaction at the peak wave vector, and near magnetic order this small difference changes the height by a large factor. Two-particle self-consistent theory reproduces the peak because its sum rule fixes its single constant interaction near this value, but for n = 0.7-0.9 at T/t = 0.14 its self-energy overestimates the local scattering rate and underestimates the momentum-dependent part. Though strong, the fluctuations are short ranged, with a correlation length of at most about two lattice spacings, and for n = 0.7-0.9 and T/t >= 0.14 the scattering rate near the Fermi surface varies by at most about 1% at fixed band energy, without hot spots. At U/t = 4 dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) reproduces the local scattering rate and quasiparticle weight within a few percent, and the nonlocal part it misses is approximately a function of the band energy. Strong spin fluctuations thus coexist with nearly isotropic quasiparticles, and the results provide a benchmark for extensions of DMFT and for spin-fluctuation theories.
summary: This work calculates momentum-resolved properties of the 3D Hubbard model using advanced diagrammatic Monte Carlo methods. It finds that strong antiferromagnetic spin fluctuations are present near half-filling but are accompanied by quasiparticles that are remarkably isotropic. The results offer a critical test case for improving theoretical descriptions like DMFT in correlated electron systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates spin fluctuations and the nature of quasiparticles in the doped three-dimensional Hubbard model, addressing the lack of controlled momentum-resolved results in this regime.
main_result: Strong spin fluctuations coexist with nearly isotropic quasiparticles in the doped 3D Hubbard model, as evidenced by the momentum-resolved self-energy calculations.
method: The study employs connected-determinant diagrammatic Monte Carlo simulations, comparing results against TPSC theory and DMFT.
model_or_system: The system is the single-band Hubbard model on a simple-cubic lattice, described by the Hamiltonian involving hopping ($t$) and on-site repulsion ($U$). Parameters are varied across doping ($n=0.4-0.95$), temperature ($T/t=0.05-0.33$), and interaction strength ($U/t=4-8$).
key_observables: Momentum-resolved self-energy, full-zone spin susceptibility, scattering rate, and quasiparticle weight.
important_parameters: Focus is placed on $U/t=4$ and doping toward half-filling ($n=0.7-0.9$) at low temperatures ($T/t=0.14$).
main_assumptions: The analysis compares results from several theoretical frameworks (CDet, TPSC, DMFT), noting that TPSC theory overestimates the local scattering rate while DMFT misses the nonlocal part.
figures_summary: The notes mention figures showing the spin-fluctuation peak moving along the nesting ridge as filling increases, and comparisons of the self-energy and susceptibilities across the Brillouin zone.
paper_structure: The paper systematically computes and compares momentum-resolved self-energies and susceptibilities using CDet Monte Carlo, contrasting these results with predictions from TPSC and DMFT theories across a wide parameter space.
why_interesting: The finding of strong spin fluctuations coexisting with nearly isotropic quasiparticles provides a crucial benchmark for extending DMFT and spin-fluctuation theories, which are central to understanding strongly correlated materials.
